The Agent Client Protocol Overview (https://www.philschmid.de/acp-overview)
agentclientprotocol.com (https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol)
What is Agent Client Protocol? (https://medium.com/@ramunarasinga/what-is-agent-client-protocol-52ce16ab8ebe)
Overview of the Agent Client Protocol architecture (https://agentclientprotocol.com/overview/architecture)
protocol overview (https://mintlify.com/agentclientprotocol/typescript-sdk/concepts/protocol-overview)
What Is the Agent Client Protocol? (https://www.morphllm.com/agent-client-protocol)
agent-client-protocol 2.0.0 (https://docs.rs/crate/agent-client-protocol/2.0.0/source/README.md)
ahp and acp (https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/guide/ahp-and-acp)
agent client protocol python (https://github.com/psiace/agent-client-protocol-python)
The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) is an open standard for how code editors talk to AI coding agents. Here's a summary of the results:

- **Origin:** It was originally published by Zed Industries in August 2025. Zed is the editor behind it, and the protocol is maintained on GitHub.
- **Purpose:** It replaces one-off editor-to-agent integrations with a shared interface, so a compliant agent can run in a compliant editor without custom glue code (ACP replaces those one-off integrations with a single interface). The Language Server Protocol is the usual comparison (The closest analogy is the Language Server Protocol.).
- **Technical basis:** Messages use JSON-RPC 2.0. They communicate over stdio (agent runs as subprocess) or HTTP (remote agents), and all communication happens over stdin/stdout in the local case.
- **Session flow:** The client starts with an initialization step, then creates or resumes a session, sends prompts, and receives streamed updates from the agent (Methods: Request-response pairs that expect a result or error, and Notifications: One-way messages that don't expect a response).
- **Permissions:** When an agent wants to take an action such as running a command or writing a file, it asks the editor for approval, which keeps the user in control (When an agent wants to run a terminal command or write a file, it sends a session/request_permission message to the editor. The editor (and by extension, the user) approves or denies each action.).
- **Versioning:** The current stable wire protocol is version 1, with schema artifacts published per version.
- **Related work:** Microsoft's Agent Host Protocol is a separate project that handles coordination of multiple clients over shared sessions. ACP covers point-to-point communication between one client and one agent (AHP is a coordination layer. ACP is a communication layer.).
- **SDKs:** Implementations exist in several languages, including Rust (the `agent-client-protocol` crate on docs.rs) and Python (A Python implementation of the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).).

Sources consulted include the official site (agentclientprotocol.com), the GitHub-hosted spec, docs.rs, and several third-party explainers. The third-party pieces are less authoritative than the official documentation.
